svg.text: Sleep timing combines circadian prediction, homeostatic sleep pressure and body context, and the resulting states feed back on those inputs. Switch circuitry is detailed in Figure 2.
melatonin feedback on the clock (MT1/MT2 receptors)
Feedback: sleep, behavior and body rhythms reset the inputs
*Sleep-linked glymphatic clearance and the synaptic homeostasis hypothesis are both actively debated; they are shown as proposed functions.
Active phase = daytime in humans; the DMH relay was mapped mainly in nocturnal rodents. Arousal groups also inhibit REM; see Figure 2.

Abbreviations: ACh, acetylcholine; ACTH, adrenocorticotropic hormone; BNST, bed nucleus of the stria terminalis; CRH, corticotropin-releasing hormone; DMH, dorsomedial hypothalamus; HPA, hypothalamic–pituitary–adrenal;

IGL, intergeniculate leaflet; ipRGCs, intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells; LC, locus coeruleus; MnPO, median preoptic nucleus; NE, noradrenaline; NPY, neuropeptide Y; NTS, nucleus of the solitary tract; PAG, periaqueductal grey;

PPT/LDT, pedunculopontine/laterodorsal tegmental nuclei; PVN, paraventricular nucleus; SCN, suprachiasmatic nucleus; TMN, tuberomammillary nucleus; TRH, thyrotropin-releasing hormone; VLPO, ventrolateral preoptic nucleus;
vSPZ, ventral subparaventricular zone; VTA, ventral tegmental area; 5-HT, serotonin.
